messages.author: fdd7f60356cd6b6d
messages.subject: reset the node color rule
parts:
HI
I am trying to reset all the color rules by:

setDefaultNodeColor(cw, '#FFFFFF', vizmap.style.name = "default")
[1] TRUE
> redraw(cw)

But this does not seem to change anything, Is this the expected behavior=?

Thanks!
-burak

messages.author: aedc8ef8f23b5716
messages.subject: Re: reset the node color rule
parts:
Hi Burak,

I've had similar experiences. It seems that Cytoscape 2.x locks in certain vizmap settings, in not always predictable ways.

For instance, if you set a visual attribute using one of the direct calls (i.e., setNodeColorDirect) then there is no way to undo it later, and go back to mapping rules.

My solution is awkward: I develop Cytoscape maps (networks, that is, with vizmapping and layout) driven all from R. When I get in a jam, as you have being unable to reset the default node color, I shut down Cytoscape, restart, and regenerate things.

It may be that a judicious use of visual styles will accomplish this end too. I'll experiment and let you know.

It's also possible that the good (& busy!) people developing Cytoscape 3 will be interested in this use case.

Cheers!

- Paul

messages.author: 12f96a26b5858610
messages.subject: Re: reset the node color rule
parts:
Hi Paul,

I think you can work around this by deleting the visual attribute of the
node for which you set a particular property. The visual mapping system
should notice this and should redraw the graph using the standard
settings of the visual mapper that you're using (you might need to redraw).

Have you tried that?

Cheers,

Jan

messages.subject: Re: reset the node color rule
parts:
Hi Jan,

I reproduced Burak's situation in a small example. Using the standard
demo network produced by makeSimpleGraph, and after setting up a
nodeColor rule:

node.types = c ('kinase', 'transcription factor', 'glycoprotein')
colors = c ('#00FFFF', '#0088FF', '#0044FF')
setNodeColorRule (cw, 'type', node.types, colors, mode='lookup')

I am unable to see an effect from this

setDefaultNodeColor (cw, '#DDAAAA'); redraw (cw)

until, in the vizmapper GUI, I click on 'Node Color' and then choose
'Delete Mapping' from the popup menu.

Forgive me if I misunderstood your reply -- you mentioned the
'delete[Node|Edge|Network]Attribute function'. Maybe in time we could
get a function like this?

deleteVizMap ('Node Color')

And perhaps something like this, too?

deleteDirectVizAssignment ('Node Color', nodes=c ('A', 'B', 'C'))

In both cases, the color of nodes would fall back to the current
default.

- Paul

messages.author: 12f96a26b5858610
messages.subject: Re: reset the node color rule
parts:
Hi Paul,

the functions you mention should not be hard to implement. I'll try to
find some time to do this after my vacation (2 weeks in France).

The function I mentioned should be able to remove one attribute for all
nodes. You need to specify the name of the attribute for that. All the
'overwrite' commands create an attribute which reflects the new value of
the visual parameter. Use the getVisualBypassNames() to get a list of
what the names are of these attributes or use the attribute browser.

Cheers,

Jan
